title: Set-Aside Account Statuses: Depletion and Closing
content:
A set-aside under Set-Aside Accounts is active when established and can move to depleted, cancelled or closed.

| From | To | When |
|---|---|---|
| Active | Depleted | A disbursement or fee draw brings the balance to 0.00 — on that same date |
| Active | Cancelled | The borrower cancelled a borrower-elected set-aside by signed request and the unused balance was released |
| Active | Closed | The set-aside's purpose was fulfilled (repairs completed) or the loan was paid in full or terminated |
| Depleted | Closed | The loan was paid in full or terminated |

## Closing rules

- **Loan termination.** A set-aside closes for loan termination only when the loan status is paid in full, claim terminated or rescinded, as the plan's closing setting provides. It closes on the loan's terminated date, and any remaining balance is released on that date with the reason "loan terminated", which restores nothing because the loan has ended.
- **Repairs completed.** A Repair Set-Aside also closes on the date its final repair draw is paid, as the repair rule sets out.
- **Depletion.** A set-aside becomes depleted on the date a disbursement or fee draw brings its balance to 0.00, and a depleted set-aside only ever moves on to closed.
- **Due and payable is not termination.** A set-aside is never closed merely because the loan became due and payable; while the loan is due and payable it keeps paying only where the plan continues paying while due and payable.

## Hypothetical readings

- A loan whose status is due and payable, with no terminated date: the set-aside stays open.
- A loan paid in full with a terminated date of 15 March: the set-aside closes on 15 March, and a remaining balance of 640.00 is released that day with the reason "loan terminated".
